posts.idea: The label: museum-style problem label carousel (4 slides, setter's own sentence, crux crop, other problems as labels)
[Colour] to move: chess-puzzle start-position carousel for first-timers
Departures: reset schedule as one flat-ground timetable card
Front desk pick: named staff member's card over a photo of one easy problem
What came down, what went up: reel from a fixed tripod position

promised_sections.note: Fully specified carousel with slide-by-slide content, failure conditions and caption job.

promised_sections.section: 2. It works in another niche. your version.
promised_sections.note: Four transfers, each with a concrete gym version. Two are refused with a stated reason.
Four ranked follow-ups with 'fails if' notes. Mostly repeats the patterns from section 2.
Six trend items with sources and dates. Skewed to industry press, and the answer says so.

promised_sections.section: 5. Well made, and what we could establish about it
promised_sections.note: Two brand identities with take/leave notes. No reach data and no screenshots, so it is thin, but the take/leave lines are usable.
A vocabulary table with sources. There is no volume column because Google Trends failed.

promised_sections.section: Research notes: gaps / inferences / pages opened
promised_sections.note: The gaps subsection mostly lists what could not be reached. The inferences are honest but are not deliverable content.

price_why: A freelance social manager would pay for the label carousel and the chess-puzzle carousel, which come with cover, slide order and hook already settled, plus the Departures card. They would not pay more, because a lot of the document is research provenance and a near-empty section 5 that they would skim past.
one_line: A research-backed creative brief for a bouldering gym that leads with one fully specified 'museum label' carousel and adds three more ready-to-build static and carousel formats borrowed from other niches.
strongest: The 'label' carousel is specified down to cover treatment, per-slide content, the no-hook decision, the caption job and what would make it fail, and it needs only a wall photo and one sentence from a setter.
weakest: The pick of the lead idea rests on trade-press trends rather than anything about this gym's members. The document is padded with source lists and a nearly empty section 5, and two source URLs are malformed, so the real substance takes digging to find.
